source.title: Clicking a tag chip in the workflow list sends `tags:[null]` → 500 "Parsed filter does not fit the schema" (still present in 2.47.7, see #24427)

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body: ### Bug Description Clicking a tag chip on a workflow card in the Workflows list fails with the toast **"Error fetching workflows — Parsed filter does not fit the schema"**. This is the same bug as #24427, which was auto-closed as stale without a fix (the linked PR #24489 was closed unmerged). It still reproduces on **2.47.7**. ### Request ``` GET /rest/workflows?includeScopes=true&filter={"isArchived":false,"tags":[null,null],"projectId":""}&skip=0&take=50&sortBy=updatedAt:desc → 500 Internal Server Error {"code":0,"message":"Parsed filter does not fit the schema"} ``` The tag IDs in the `filter` query param are serialized as `null`, so the chip click handler appears to be reading an undefined `id` from the card's tag objects. The backend filter schema expects an array of strings and rejects it, but returns 500 rather than 400. ### Screenshots ### To Reproduce 1. Open a project's Workflows list 2. Click a tag chip on any tagged workflow card 3. Error toast "Error fetching workflows — Parsed filter does not fit the schema" 4. In DevTools > Network, the `/rest/workflows` request has `"tags":[null,...]` in the `filter` param and returns 500 ### Expected behavior Clicking a tag chip filters the workflow list to workflows with that tag. Additionally, an invalid filter should return a 400 instead of a 500. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.47.7 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 26.13.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: postgres - executionMode: scaling (multi-main) - concurrency: -1 ### Operating System Linux (Docker) ### n8n Version 2.47.7 ### Node.js Version 26.13.0 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode queue ### Hosting self hosted

comments.author: Murad-khan-professional
comments.text:
Hi! I'd like to work on this if it's open for a community contribution.

I traced it on current `master`:

- `onClickTag` (`packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/views/WorkflowsView.vue` ~L1065) pushes the tag **id** into `filters.tags` and calls `fetchWorkflows()`.
- `fetchWorkflows` (~L910) converts ids to names with `tagsStore.tagsById[tagId]?.name`. If the tags store hasn't been loaded, that yields `undefined`, which serializes as `null` → `"tags":[null]` → the backend schema rejects it with a 500.
- The store is only loaded via `tagsStore.fetchAll()` in the query-string path (~L1155, when the page is opened with `?tags=` in the URL), so clicking a chip on a fresh load hits the empty store. That also explains why the old fix in #24489 (filtering out `undefined`) wasn't right: it would hide the error but silently drop the filter.

Plan:
1. Make sure the tag name is resolved before fetching: load the tags store in `onClickTag` (it's cached, so cheap), and ideally fall back to the tag name from the clicked workflow card, which already has it.
2. Never send `null`/`undefined` entries in the `tags` filter.
3. Add regression tests in `WorkflowsView.test.ts`: clicking a tag chip with an empty tags store sends the tag name (not `null`), and the URL `?tags=` path still works.

One question: `tagsStore.fetchAll()` returns `[]` when the user lacks the global `tag:list` scope (`tags.store.ts` ~L98). Is a project member without that scope expected to filter by tag here? If so, using the name from the workflow card (step 1 fallback) is what would make it work for them, so I'd include that unless you prefer otherwise.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: One detail for the proposed fix: `tagsStore.fetchAll()` returns `[]` when the viewer lacks the `tag:list` scope, so loading it in `onClickTag` would still leave the clicked ID unresolved for those viewers. `WorkflowCard.vue` already has the tag objects but currently emits only `tagId` in its `click:tag` event. Passing the clicked tag name along with its ID would let `WorkflowsView` build the API filter from the card data without requiring `tag:list`; the filter should still avoid sending unresolved entries.
